draftA:
REQ-1 For each distributor and product, calculate days of cover as stock on hand divided by average daily sell-out. Average daily sell-out is the distributor's total sell-out over the last 4 weeks (28 days) divided by 28.
REQ-2 Raise an alert when days of cover is below 7, meaning the distributor is likely to run out within a week. Assumption to confirm with National sales operations: exactly 7.0 days does not trigger an alert.
REQ-3 Send the alert to the area sales manager responsible for the distributor, at most once per distributor per product per day.
REQ-4 In v1, seasonal products follow the same rule as all other products; separate seasonal handling is logged as a proposal only. Assumption to confirm: if 4-week sell-out is zero, days of cover is undefined and no alert is sent.
AC-1 Given stock on hand of 120 units and 4-week sell-out of 560 units, average daily sell-out is 560 / 28 = 20, so days of cover is 120 / 20 = 6.0. Because 6.0 is below 7, the area sales manager receives an alert.
AC-2 Given stock on hand of 300 units and 4-week sell-out of 840 units, average daily sell-out is 840 / 28 = 30, so days of cover is 300 / 30 = 10.0. Because 10.0 is not below 7, no alert is sent.
AC-3 Given the AC-1 case is evaluated twice on the same day, the area sales manager receives exactly one alert for that distributor and product that day. If the condition still holds the next day, one new alert is sent.
AC-4 Given stock on hand of 140 units and 4-week sell-out of 560 units, days of cover is 140 / 20 = 7.0. No alert is sent, per the REQ-2 boundary assumption.
draftB:
REQ-1. Alert the area sales manager in the distributor portal when a distributor is likely to run out of a product within a week.
REQ-2. Treat likely to run out as days of cover of 7 or less, calculated as stock on hand divided by average daily sales.
REQ-3. Calculate average daily sales as the last 4 weeks of distributor sell-out divided by 28 days.
REQ-4. Raise at most one alert per distributor per product per day.
REQ-5. Do not apply a separate seasonal rule in v1; flag that change as a proposal only.
AC-1. If the last 4 weeks of sell-out total 28, average daily sales is 1; stock on hand of 7 gives days of cover of 7 and the alert is raised.
AC-2. If average daily sales is 1 and stock on hand is 8, days of cover is 8 and no alert is raised.
AC-3. If an alert for that distributor and product was already raised today, no further alert is raised that day.

findings.title: Seven days cover excluded
findings.detail: The brief alerts when a distributor is likely to run out within a week. Cover of exactly 7 days means stock lasts a week, so that case is inside the window. Alerting only below 7, and testing no alert at 7.0, drops it before the assumption is confirmed.
findings.quote: exactly 7.0 days does not trigger an alert

reviewOfA.strengths: The worked examples recompute correctly, and audience, daily cap, and seasonal treatment match the requester's answers.

findings.title: Zero sales case undefined
findings.detail: If the last 4 weeks of sell-out total 0, average daily sales is 0 and stock divided by 0 is undefined. No requirement or acceptance criterion says whether an alert is raised, suppressed or errors. Add a rule and a test for this case.
findings.quote: calculated as stock on hand divided by average daily sales.

findings.title: Fast-moving scope not addressed
findings.detail: The task targets fast-moving products, but the requirements apply to every product with no definition or filter. Either confirm all products are in scope or ask the requester how fast-moving is defined.
findings.quote: when a distributor is likely to run out of a product within a week.

reviewOfB.strengths: The acceptance criteria compute correctly (28/28 = 1; 7/1 = 7 raises an alert; 8/1 = 8 does not) and test the boundary on both sides of the 7-day threshold.

merge.document:
REQ-1 For each distributor and product, calculate days of cover as stock on hand divided by average daily sell-out. Average daily sell-out is the distributor's total sell-out over the last 4 weeks (28 days) divided by 28.
REQ-2 Raise an alert when days of cover is 7 or less, meaning the distributor is likely to run out within a week.
REQ-3 Send the alert in the distributor portal to the area sales manager responsible for the distributor, at most once per distributor per product per day.
REQ-4 In v1, seasonal products follow the same rule as all other products. Separate seasonal handling is logged as a proposal only.
REQ-5 Assumption to confirm with National sales operations: if 4-week sell-out is zero, days of cover is undefined and no alert is sent.
REQ-6 Assumption to confirm with National sales operations: v1 covers all products, because no definition of fast-moving was given. Ask the requester how fast-moving is defined if a filter is needed.
AC-1 Given stock on hand of 120 units and 4-week sell-out of 560 units, average daily sell-out is 560 / 28 = 20, so days of cover is 120 / 20 = 6.0. Because 6.0 is 7 or less, the area sales manager receives an alert.
AC-2 Given stock on hand of 140 units and 4-week sell-out of 560 units, days of cover is 140 / 20 = 7.0. Because 7.0 is 7 or less, an alert is sent.
AC-3 Given stock on hand of 160 units and 4-week sell-out of 560 units, days of cover is 160 / 20 = 8.0. Because 8.0 is above 7, no alert is sent.
AC-4 Given the AC-1 case is evaluated twice on the same day, the area sales manager receives exactly one alert for that distributor and product that day. If the condition still holds the next day, one new alert is sent.
AC-5 Given stock on hand of 50 units and 4-week sell-out of 0 units, days of cover is undefined, no alert is sent and no error is raised.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's structure: explicit formula, named recipient, worked examples with real unit counts, the repeat-alert test, and the zero-sales assumption.
merge.keptFromB: I kept draft B's 7-or-less threshold, its test of both sides of the boundary, and its explicit mention of alert delivery in the distributor portal.

resolutions.note: The threshold is now 7 or less, matching the brief's 'within a week'. AC-2 now expects an alert at 7.0 (140 / 20). AC-3 adds the no-alert case at 8.0 (160 / 20).
REQ-5 states that zero 4-week sell-out means no alert and no error, flagged as an assumption to confirm. AC-5 tests this case.
REQ-6 puts all products in scope for v1, because the requester gave no definition of fast-moving. It is flagged for confirmation, with a question on the definition if a filter is wanted.
